extracted.intended_audience: attorneys registered to practice before the USPTO / patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing practitioner conduct, remediation, sanctions, and notice in USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline disciplinary matters. Focused on fiduciary/accounting duties, honesty in USPTO transactions, remediation steps, and the procedural mechanics of stayed suspensions/probation and show-cause proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain separate client trust and business/operating accounts (no commingling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.112(a) and (b) by not maintaining separate accounts for client funds and business/operating expenses and for commingling client and business funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit only client funds into a client trust (IOLTA) account; maintain a separate account for business/operating transactions. The notice describes establishing a client trust account into which only client funds are deposited and a separate business/operating account as required remedial action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain complete accounting records for client funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.112(c)(3) by not maintaining complete records of client funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep formal accounting records/ledgers for fiduciary transactions. The respondent instituted a manual ledger and purchased software capable of performing ledger functions for both client trust and operating accounts, and must reconcile accounts monthly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misrepresentation in transactions with the USPTO (no insufficient-funds submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent engaged in conduct involving misrepresentation by submitting checks to the USPTO that were drawn on insufficient funds in violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure checks/payments to the USPTO are supported by sufficient funds. If notified of returned checks, promptly make good on outstanding fees and any late/untimely payment fees, as the respondent did after notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conduct that adversely reflects on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting checks that were returned for insufficient funds constitutes conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice under 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner conduct that undermines trust in professional fitness (e.g., financial mismanagement resulting in returned checks) is sanctionable; maintain financial practices that preserve professional fitness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement remedial practice-management measures when deficiencies identified
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent took remedial steps (establish trust/account separation, use ledger, purchase practice/financial management software, adopt new fee/engagement/closing letters, implement checklists and monthly reconciliations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended/required remediation includes: establishing separate accounts, using manual or software-led ledgers, acquiring practice and financial software capable of ledger functions, adopting written engagement/closing letters (reviewed by competent counsel/consultant), instituting financial and USPTO transactional checklists, and monthly reconciliation of trust and operating accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion and documentation of required continuing legal education
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the discipline, Respondent must purchase and complete the online CLE class 'IOLTA Accounts and Retainer Agreements' approved by the Illinois State Bar Association within 90 days, and provide an affidavit and documentation evidencing receipt of CLE credit within 120 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the specified course within the deadline, obtain CLE credit documentation, and submit an affidavit and supporting documentation to the OED Director as proof of compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning structure: stayed suspension with probation and conditional activation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for 24 months, the entirety of which is immediately stayed, and respondent is placed on a 24-month probation. The stay remains in effect unless lifted by order of the USPTO Director or his designate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stay allows continued practice during probation unless the stay is lifted; if the stay is not lifted by the end of probation, the respondent will not serve the suspension. This illustrates the Office's ability to impose stayed suspensions conditioned on probationary compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show-cause procedure and possible lifting of stay for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the respondent failed to comply with the Final Order or Disciplinary Rules during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to respondent's last address, grant 15 days to respond, and if noncompliance is still believed, deliver the Order to Show Cause, respondent's response, and evidence to the USPTO Director to request lifting the stay and imposing suspension up to 24 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural steps: (1) Issue Order to Show Cause; (2) send to address of record; (3) allow 15 days to respond; (4) if still believed noncompliant, forward materials to USPTO Director requesting immediate lifting of stay and suspension. The Order to Show Cause can lead to immediate suspension if the stay is lifted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and publication requirements for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and publish a Notice of Stayed Suspension in the Official Gazette; the OED Director shall give notice of public discipline and the reasons pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final disciplinary actions are publicly disclosed via the OED Reading Room and Official Gazette, including the factual basis and rules violated; practitioners should expect public notice of discipline and its reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on applicability of certain rules unless stay lifted
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60 do not apply unless the stay of the suspension is lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific procedural rules concerning suspension/appeal apply only if the stayed suspension is activated; practitioners should note which regulations become operative if and when a stay is lifted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, shall be considered (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding (a) as an aggravating factor in determining discipline and/or (b) to rebut statements or representations by or on respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior disciplinary findings can aggravate sanctions in later matters and can be used to rebut claims; maintain compliance to avoid future aggravation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties bear their own costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement terms may allocate costs to each party independently rather than imposing cost recovery by the Office in this matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional and regulatory basis for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20(a)(2), 11.20(a)(4), and 11.26; the Proposed Settlement Agreement satisfies 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 and the action is pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.26 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions are taken under specific statutory and regulatory authority; settlement agreements must satisfy 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 requirements and are subject to Director approval. Practitioners should be aware of these governing provisions.
